beats.narration: Checkpoint two: three contributions, and two matches for each — the channel built for it, and the readiness item it's missing. If you haven't made your matches, pause here first.

Case A, the focused API wrapper: it goes to the tool's own repository, and what's missing is a test proving the wrapper behaves — focused isn't enough by itself. Case B, the full customer-service application: it fits no channel whole. The reusable pattern has to be stripped out first, and only that focused example goes to the Cookbook. Case C, the one-line fix carried from an engagement: it goes to the example's own repository, and what's missing is the rights check — engagement code can carry a licensing constraint that blocks the merge before any technical review even starts.

elements.code:
A  API wrapper  → tool's own repo        + a test
B  full app     → strip the pattern      → Cookbook
C  1-line fix   → example's own repo     + rights check

elements.text:
B is the trap: a whole app fits nowhere —
only the extracted pattern travels
C: licensing blocks BEFORE technical review

beats.narration: The coupling is the lesson: the channel follows the contribution's shape, and readiness fills what the maintainer can't verify. A wrong channel stalls regardless of quality — and a missing rights check can un-merge a merge. Next: requirements and lifecycle.

readiness fills the verify-gap
